note: A real Postgres 17's own answer to the timeline keyset order, recorded so the
browser's copy of that order can be replayed against it without a database.
Generated by inserting 400 random (timestamptz, uuid) pairs plus nine chosen
ties into a table and reading them back with the read path's own clause --
the wire renders it (Date#toISOString, millisecond precision).
The chosen ties all share one instant and exist to exercise the uuid half at the
boundaries a STRING comparison could get wrong where Postgres's BYTE comparison
does not: uuids starting with a digit against uuids starting with a letter,
all-zeroes, all-f, and the 0f/10 and 99/a0 crossings.
order: descending -- index 0 is the newest slot, which is the top of page one
